tldr: NVIDIA unveiled Nemotron 3 Ultra — a frontier reasoning model — alongside Cosmos 3 and the RTX Spark in early June. Two days later it was available to deploy on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, where AWS pitched roughly 5x faster inference and 30% lower cost for agentic AI workloads. The thread traces a fast announcement-to-cloud-availability path for a model aimed squarely at agentic reasoning.
whats_new: Nemotron 3 Ultra moved from announcement to one-deploy cloud availability on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart within two days, with AWS quoting 5x faster inference and 30% lower cost for agentic workloads.
why_it_matters: For platform engineers the signal isn't the launch but the deployment path: a frontier reasoning model reachable through SageMaker JumpStart with vendor-quoted inference and cost wins makes it cheap to A/B against incumbents for agentic workloads.

status.detail: Announced Jun 2 alongside Cosmos 3 and the RTX Spark; available to deploy on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart by Jun 4.

beats.headline: Nemotron 3 Ultra unveiled with Cosmos 3 and the RTX Spark
beats.summary: NVIDIA introduces Nemotron 3 Ultra, a frontier reasoning model, as part of an early-June launch roundup.

beats.headline: Deployable on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart — 5x faster inference, 30% lower cost
beats.summary: AWS makes Nemotron 3 Ultra deployable on SageMaker JumpStart, pitching it for agentic AI workloads.

open_questions: Do the 5x inference / 30% cost figures hold up in independent benchmarks?
Which other clouds (Bedrock, Azure, Vertex) pick up Nemotron 3 Ultra, and when?
How does Nemotron 3 Ultra compare with incumbent frontier reasoning models on agentic tasks?
take_for_builders: If you run agentic reasoning workloads on AWS, Nemotron 3 Ultra is now a one-deploy A/B candidate on SageMaker JumpStart — worth a cost/latency bake-off against your current model before committing.
